caseno: Writ Petition No. 534 of 1977. In the matter of: An application under Article 102 (3) ( a) (ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
lawyer:
Shah Md. Sharif with Fakhrul Islam, Md. Wahidullah ----- For the Petitioner. 
Syed J. R. Mudassir Hossain, A. A. G. ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Nasiruddin Sarkar ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Member,  Appellate Tribunal and others ------Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The petitioner was prosecuted on a First Information Report lodged by an Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police, (PW. 1) attached to Tongi Police Station. It was alleged there in that the Asstt. Sub-Inspector of Police while returning from a village called Ghutia in the evening of 3.12.75 and passing by the side of the house of one Jamiruddin of Palasona found about 15/20 persons discussing something in a suspicious manner. At the sight of the police all those persons except one, namely accused Nasiruddin (Petitioner) ran away; Nasiruddin was arrested and on search of his body a pistol with 3 cartridges was recovered from him which were then seized in the presence of witnesses including two constables who accompanied the Asstt. S.I. of Police. But while returning to the Thana the arrested person was snatched away by other miscreants. On this First Information Report the Police investigated the-case and submitted charge sheet against the petitioner who was then put on trial under the Special Powers Act. He pleaded not guilty taking the defence that he was never arrested at the alleged time and place nor was any arm or ammunition recovered from his possession but he was falsely implicated at the instance of one Kazi Zafar, President of Sramik Federation out of his grudge against him (accused) who was a leader of the rival Workers Union, Sramik League. The learned Special Tribunal on consideration of the evidence of 7 witnesses for the prosecution there having been no witness examined by the defense, held the accused guilty and convicted and sentenced him as aforesaid. The learned Appellate Tribunal after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal confirming the order of conviction and sentence. 

 4. Mr. Shah Md. Sharif, the learned Advocate who has appeared for the petitioner has referred to the judgment of both the Courts below as well as to the evidence on record. On perusal of these papers it is found that the Courts below accepted the evidence as given by the witness without shifting them of the witnesses P. W. I am the complainant Asstt. SI of Police, P.W. 4 is one of the two constables who bad accompanied P. W. I on the journey, P. Ws. 2 and 3 are members of the public who had also accompanied P.W. I as guides on the journey from Gutia to Tongi P.S. Their evidence is that P. W. 1 accompanied by P. W. 4 and another constable was returning from Gutia, where he had held an enquiry, towards his Thana Hoq, but on the way while passing by the house of one Zamiruddin of village Palasona he came across 15/20 persons discussing something In front of the house; all these persons except the accused ran away; that this accused was arrested on the spot and from his person a pistol with three cartridges was recovered ; these articles were seized under a seizure list but on the way the accused was snatched away by some miscreants. The defense case is that there was no such incident at all in the house of Zamiruddin and that the case is concocted. Neither Zamiruddin nor any member of his house was examined in this case. It was explained that as the miscreants were suspected in his house he was not expected to depose in this case. But no explanation was offered as to why not a single neighbor or co-villager of Zahiruddin was examined in this case, at least to give support to the prosecution story that any occurrence like arrest of a miscreant with fire-arms took place in Zahiruddin's house. The two guides, P.Ws. 2 and 3 are not residents of Palasona, they are residents of village Gutia 2 miles away; evidence on record shows that there were 300/400 families in Zamiruddin's village. Now, as to the incident itself, though P.W. stated in deposition that he was present with P.W. 1 at the time of arrest of the accused and recovery of the pistol and he had seen about 15/20 persons with the accused in Zahiruddin's house, in cross-examination he stated that he did not see any person with the accused because of darkness". As to the articles recovered from the accused, he said that he did not see what article was recovered" but P.W. I produced before him a pistol saying it was recovered from the accused. This evidence was not challenged by the prosecution P.W. 4 accepted the defense suggestion that Kazi Zafar was the leader of one Worker's Union while the accused was the leader of another group of Workers. P W. 7 (10) admitted that there were rival groups of workers, one Sramik League, and the other Sramik Federation and that these groups were fighting with each other. As to the Arms Expert, P.W. 6, he said that he had examined a pistol bearing no. 1124681, but the ejahar shows that the pistol recovered by P.W. I bear No. 112581. As to the accused, though be was arrested on the spot as claimed by P.W. I he was not produced to the Thana on the plea that he was snatched away. When there was a police party who also got possession of a loaded pistol, it should have been considered by the Courts below how the arrested person could have been snatched away. Moreover, it is this accused against whom, as the prosecution, case shows was wanted in connection with another case and it is this accused who along remained on the spot while all others fled away. No attempt was made by the police to trace out those persons including Zahiruddin during the investigation. These are vital points and non-consideration of these points by the Courts below caused miscarriage of justice. Though the trial was held under a special law, the courts below were not relieved of their duty to follow the fundamental principles of criminal trials which are that the accused shall be presumed to be innocent and it is the prosecution which shall prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Non-observance of these basic principles is an error of law and this Court in its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution has got power to see whether an order of conviction has been based on legal evidence which necessarily includes consideration of material points, probability and circumstance of each case. 

 5. In the result the rule is made absolute and the impugned order of conviction and sentence is declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect. The order of conviction and sentence is set aside and the case is sent back to the Appellate Tribunal for rehearing and disposal of the appeal expeditiously, in any case within six weeks from this order.
